note.text: Determiners help specify a noun phrase. Articles distinguish uses such as a new proposal and the proposal already identified. The choice of a or an follows the next sound in the selected pronunciation, not simply its first letter: an hour but a useful guide. Quantifiers express amount or number; possessive forms identify a relationship. Countability depends on use: information is uncountable in the model, while an item of information is countable.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to choose a determiner that fits reference, countability and meaning. Builds on: noun phrases and prior quantifiers. Leads to: precise description and summary.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: Determiners help specify a noun phrase. Articles distinguish uses such as a new proposal and the proposal already identified. The choice of a or an follows the next sound in the selected pronunciation, not simply its first letter: an hour but a useful guide. Quantifiers express amount or number; possessive forms identify a relationship. Countability depends on use: information is uncountable in the model, while an item of information is countable.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: Bih read a proposal. The proposal concerned our library and requested some information. A introduces an unspecified proposal; the points back to the identified one; our marks a relationship; some fits the uncountable use of information. These choices guide the reader’s reference rather than merely decorating the noun.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify the noun and intended reference. Test countability in this use, the next sound for a/an and whether possession or quantity is intended. Do not combine incompatible determiners merely because each can occur elsewhere.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: An must precede every word beginning with a vowel letter. Correction: The next sound, rather than the letter alone, determines a or an.
The always means the referent is unknown to everyone. Correction: Context can identify a referent.
Many information is the taught ordinary pattern. Correction: Many fits plural countable nouns, not this use of information.
Our and ours are interchangeable before library. Correction: Our precedes the noun; ours can stand independently.

pick.q: Choose the model article: ___ hour remained.
e: Hour begins with a vowel sound in this model.
Hour is singular here.

pick.q: Choose the model article: It is ___ useful guide.
e: Useful begins with a consonant /j/ sound in this model.
Guide is singular here.
Ours does not determine guide this way.
pick.y: Use a before the consonant onset in useful.

pick.q: Choose the ordinary uncountable pattern: We need ___.
e: Use an item of information for a countable unit.

A few requires plural countable items.
